analyses.name: Liquidia Corporation
analyses.verdict: A commercial-stage inflection story with the cleanest chart in the scan — Yutrepia's ramp is turning a development-stage cost base into real revenue, and both my read and TradingView's agree without reservation.

financials.summary: FY2025 was the transition year from development-stage to commercial. Liquidia spent most of its history as a pre-revenue respiratory specialist funded by equity raises and a Sandoz-partnered generic treprostinil injection; the FY2025 income statement still shows a substantial net loss driven by SG&A build-out for the Yutrepia sales force and continued R&D, offset by the first meaningful product revenue. The balance sheet was recapitalised through the year to fund the launch, so the share count is materially higher than it was two years ago. Cash flow from operations remained negative — the entire investment case rests on the revenue trajectory outrunning that burn, which is exactly what the scan's revenue-growth reading of +4,158% year over year reflects. Live figures render in the TradingView financials widget alongside this note.
highlights: Revenue growth of roughly +4,158% year over year off a near-zero base — the Yutrepia launch inflection
Forward P/E of 14.9 despite the growth rate, because the market is pricing forward earnings power, not trailing losses
Market cap $7.7B against that revenue base — the valuation is entirely a function of launch execution
Operating cash flow still negative; the funding runway is the number to track each quarter
Street analyst rating of 1.38 — near-unanimous buy coverage

accomplishments: Won the regulatory and legal path to market for Yutrepia (treprostinil inhalation powder) after a multi-year patent fight with the incumbent
Built and deployed a specialty pulmonary sales organisation from scratch and converted it into a commercial ramp within the first full year
Maintained the Sandoz-partnered generic treprostinil injection as a secondary revenue stream through the transition
Stock advanced from a 52-week low of 17.68 to 86.80 — roughly a five-fold move — on execution rather than promotion

journey_52w.summary: One of the great re-ratings of the past year. Liquidia entered the period as a contested small-cap whose entire value hinged on an appellate outcome, traded as low as 17.68, then re-rated relentlessly as the legal overhang lifted and the launch data began arriving. The stock is now 2.5% from its 52-week high of 89.03, with the 50-day at 72.77 and the 200-day at 44.63 — the moving-average fan is as wide as it gets, and the stock has still spent the last several weeks building a tight 5-contraction consolidation rather than blowing off.

analyses.name: Apple Inc.
analyses.verdict: The best-positioned megacap chart in a broken tech tape — but it reports tomorrow into a memory-cost squeeze, so the setup is real and the timing is not.

financials.summary: Apple's last full fiscal year was another record, driven less by unit growth than by mix and Services. The hardware business remains the revenue anchor, with iPhone the largest single line, while Services — the App Store, iCloud, advertising, payments and licensing — continued to grow faster than hardware and at a far higher gross margin, which is what has been lifting the blended company margin for several years. Operating cash flow remained enormous and was returned aggressively through buybacks and the dividend, shrinking the share count and flattering EPS growth above revenue growth. The scan reads trailing EPS growth of +21.8% against revenue growth of +16.6% — that gap is the buyback and the Services mix at work. Live statements render in the TradingView financials widget below.
highlights: EPS growth of +21.8% outpacing revenue growth of +16.6% — Services mix plus buyback
Services remains the margin engine and the reason the blended gross margin keeps climbing

analyses.name: JP Morgan Chase & Co.
analyses.verdict: The highest-quality expression of the financials rotation, with 75 clean sessions before the next earnings event — quality plus a clear calendar is a rare combination right now.

financials.summary: FY2025 was another record year for JPMorgan across essentially every segment. Net interest income remained the largest single earnings driver, supported by a deposit base and loan book that grew through the period, while the Corporate & Investment Bank benefited from a recovery in capital-markets and advisory activity that had been depressed in prior years. Asset & Wealth Management continued compounding fee revenue, and consumer credit costs, while normalising off unusually low levels, stayed manageable. Capital ratios remained comfortably above requirements, which funded both the dividend and a substantial buyback. The scan reads EPS growth of +46.9% and revenue growth of +30.4% — a reflection of the capital-markets recovery layered on top of a resilient net-interest-income base. financials.summary: Assurant is a specialty insurer rather than a traditional life or P&C carrier — its two engines are Global Lifestyle (mobile device protection, extended warranties, vehicle protection) and Global Housing (lender-placed homeowners insurance and renters products). FY2025 saw both segments grow, with Global Housing benefiting from favourable pricing and a comparatively benign catastrophe experience relative to prior years, and Global Lifestyle grinding out fee-based growth from connected-device programmes with the large carriers. The economics are fee-and-service heavy rather than pure underwriting float, which makes earnings less volatile than a standard P&C book — until a catastrophe year arrives. analyses.name: DaVita Inc.
analyses.verdict: Up 54% in three months and 0.9% from its high, yet RSI is only 58.8 and volume has dried to 45% of average — momentum without froth, at 13.9x forward earnings.

financials.summary: DaVita operates one of the two national dialysis platforms in the United States. The economics are simple and durable: a large fixed clinic base, a patient population that cannot defer treatment, and a revenue mix split between low-margin government reimbursement (Medicare) and high-margin commercial insurance — with profitability driven almost entirely by that commercial mix. FY2025 saw treatment volumes recover toward trend, revenue per treatment rise with rate updates, and cost per treatment held in check, which is what produced the outsized earnings leverage. DaVita also runs a large, consistent buyback funded by free cash flow, so share count reduction adds meaningfully to EPS growth. The scan reads EPS growth of +43.5% on revenue growth of +6.0% — the gap is mix, cost control and the buyback. Live statements render in the TradingView financials widget below.

analyses.name: Progyny, Inc.
analyses.verdict: 70.6% EPS growth at a 14.0x forward multiple with TradingView at 15 buy / 1 sell — a small-cap with large-cap technical structure.

financials.summary: Progyny sells fertility and family-building benefits to large self-insured employers, sitting between the employer, the patient and a curated network of fertility clinics. The model is a per-employee-per-month fee plus utilisation-based revenue, so growth comes from two places: adding new employer clients, and existing clients' employees actually using the benefit. FY2025 was a year of margin repair rather than top-line expansion — the scan reads revenue growth of just +1.4% against EPS growth of +70.6%, which tells you the story precisely: the client base was roughly flat, but cost management and utilisation mix drove profitability sharply higher. The balance sheet carries no meaningful debt and the company generates cash. Live statements render in the TradingView financials widget below.

analyses.verdict: The clearest multi-year backlog in industrials, coiling 4% below its high with buyers absorbing supply at 119% of average volume.

financials.summary: Howmet makes engineered metal products for aerospace — jet engine airfoils and turbine components, fastening systems, forged aluminium wheels and structural parts. The engine-products segment is the profit engine, and its economics are unusually attractive because the aftermarket (spare parts for engines already in service) carries much higher margin than original-equipment shipments, and grows with flight hours rather than new-aircraft deliveries. FY2025 saw both legs work: commercial aerospace build rates recovered while the installed fleet flew more, lifting spares demand. Pricing discipline on long-term agreements and operating leverage on a fixed-asset-heavy base produced margin expansion well ahead of revenue growth. The scan reads EPS growth of +71.4% on revenue growth of +19.1%. Live statements render in the TradingView financials widget below.

analyses.verdict: The highest-probability pre-breakout signature in the scan: a 3-contraction coil on volume dried to 45% of average — though at 41.5x, the price is the argument against it.

financials.summary: Terreno owns industrial real estate in six coastal US markets — Northern New Jersey/New York, Los Angeles, Miami, San Francisco Bay Area, Seattle and Washington DC. The strategy is deliberately narrow: infill, last-mile logistics properties in supply-constrained submarkets where new construction is effectively impossible. That scarcity is what drives the re-leasing spreads, which have historically been among the strongest in the REIT universe. FY2025 saw continued rent growth on lease expirations, high occupancy, and accretive acquisitions funded by a conservatively levered balance sheet — Terreno runs materially less debt than most industrial REIT peers. The scan reads EPS growth of +40.2% and revenue growth of +12.7%. Live statements render in the TradingView financials widget below.

analyses.name: Datadog, Inc.
analyses.verdict: The one technology name genuinely leading this tape — up 103% in three months yet consolidated back to RSI 57.4 with relative strength at new highs.

financials.summary: Datadog sells a unified observability platform — infrastructure monitoring, application performance monitoring, log management, security monitoring and increasingly AI/LLM observability — consumed on a usage basis. That consumption model is the key to the financials: revenue scales with customers' cloud footprints, so as workloads grow, so does Datadog's take, without a new sales cycle. FY2025 delivered continued 30%-plus revenue growth with strong gross margins characteristic of a software platform, expanding operating margin as sales-and-marketing efficiency improved, and substantial free cash flow. The land-and-expand motion showed up as growth in the number of customers using four or more products. The scan reads revenue growth of +32.2% and EPS growth of +104.0%. analyses.name: NetApp, Inc.
analyses.verdict: Priced like legacy storage at 17.7x forward, trading like AI infrastructure at +57.5% in three months — with 35 clean days before the next earnings event.

financials.summary: NetApp sells enterprise data storage — all-flash arrays for on-premise workloads plus a set of first-party storage services embedded in the major public clouds. Two things matter in the financials. First, the mix shift toward all-flash, which carries better economics than the legacy hybrid systems it replaces. Second, the public-cloud storage services, which are subscription revenue and re-rate the multiple if they grow fast enough. The most recent full fiscal year showed continued all-flash growth, disciplined operating expense, healthy gross margin, and strong free cash flow returned via buyback and dividend. The scan reads revenue growth of +12.5% and EPS growth of +23.4% — the gap again being margin plus share count. Live statements render in the TradingView financials widget below.

analyses.name: SiriusXM Holdings Inc.
analyses.verdict: Just reported record-low churn and raised guidance — the gap risk is gone, the multiple is 9.1x, and 18.3% of the float is still short.

financials.summary: SiriusXM runs two businesses: the satellite radio subscription service, which is a high-margin, low-growth cash machine embedded in new vehicles, and Pandora, an ad-supported streaming business with weaker economics. The investment case has nothing to do with growth — the scan reads revenue growth of just +1.1% — and everything to do with cash conversion and capital structure. The satellite business converts subscription revenue into free cash flow at a very high rate because the infrastructure cost is largely fixed and already built. FY2025 saw management prioritise cost reduction, subscriber quality over subscriber count, and debt paydown alongside the dividend. EPS growth of +21.8% on flat revenue is what cost discipline and a shrinking share count produce. Live statements render in the TradingView financials widget below.
highlights: EPS growth of +21.8% on revenue growth of just +1.1% — entirely cost discipline and capital structure
